jina: Power to proclaim state of emergency
maudhui: (1) Subject to this Constitution or to any law enacted by Parliament in that behalf, the President may proclaim a state of emergency in the United Republic or in any part thereof. (2) The President may only proclaim a state of emergency if - (a) the United Republic is at war; (b) there is a real danger that the United Republic is about to be invaded and to be in a state of war; (c) there is an actual breakdown of public order and public safety in the United Republic or in any part thereof to such an extent as to require the taking of extraordinary measures to restore order and safety; (d) there is a clear and present danger of an actual breakdown of public order and public safety in the United Republic or any part thereof which cannot be avoided except through the taking of extraordinary measures; (e) there is imminent occurrence of danger, disaster or environmental calamity which threatens the society or part thereof in the United Republic; or (f) there is some kind of danger which clearly constitutes a threat to the state. (3) If a state of emergency is proclaimed in relation to the whole of the United Republic, or to the whole of Mainland Tanzania or the whole of Tanzania Zanzibar, the President shall forthwith transmit a copy of the proclamation to the Speaker of the National Assembly who, after consultation with the Leader of Government Business in the National Assembly, shall convene a meeting of the National Assembly within not more than fourteen days to consider the situation and decide whether or not to pass a resolution, which shall be supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all the Members, approving the proclamation of a state of emergency issued by the President. (4) Parliament may enact a law providing for the times and procedure which will enable certain persons in charge of specified functions of the Government in specified areas of the United Republic to request the President to exercise the powers conferred upon him by this Article in relation to any of those areas if there is an actual or imminent breakdown of public order and public safety in any of those areas and the breakdown cannot be avoided except through the taking of extraordinary measures. (5) A proclamation of a state of emergency issued by the President shall cease to have effect - (a) if it is revoked by the President; (b) if fourteen days elapse from the date of the proclamation without a resolution referred to in subarticle (3) being passed; (c) if it is annulled by the National Assembly by a resolution supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all the Members; or (d) upon the expiration of six months from the date of the proclamation; save that a sitting of the National Assembly may, before the expiration of six months, extend the period of the operation of the proclamation for further periods of six months at a time by a resolution supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all the Members. (6) For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of this Article shall not authorize the President to proclaim a state of emergency in relation to that part of the United Republic which is Tanzania Zanzibar, except in accordance with the Constitution of Zanzibar.
